correctness.rationale: Every MEG-subset of a cycle is exactly a cyclic gap composition with all positive gaps <n/2. Any longer gap cannot be in a unique shortest path between selected endpoints; shorter gaps themselves furnish unique shortest paths covering all edges. Marking a selected first vertex gives coefficient n/m. Deleting a selected vertex merges adjacent gaps; the resulting necessary/sufficient minimality inequalities force triples for odd cycles and triples or antipodal-pair quadruples for even cycles. Three-gap bounded-composition inclusion/exclusion gives exact coefficients. A fresh direct BFS verifier tests every vertex subset on C3 through C16 and prints VERIFY_OK; checks corroborate but are not the proof.

value.rationale: The complete labeled-subset generating function addresses the natural monitoring-network question of how many feasible placements exist at every probe budget, not just the minimum. The independent irredundant-set polynomial quantifies probe indispensability and exhibits a strict even/odd structural boundary: infinitely many even cycles support minimal but non-optimal four-probe arrangements, all exactly unions of antipodal pairs, whereas odd cycles do not. This structural classification and count is neither a mere restatement of the known scalar minimum nor an arbitrary parameter slice.
